hero.lead: An island nation of 1.4 million in the eastern Mediterranean, with €1.02 billion of EU recovery and resilience grants and growth of 2.9% projected this year.

capital.heading: An island in recovery, and every drop treated.

record.text: Recovery and resilience plan, all in grants, of which €52.4 million from REPowerEU and €52.1 million from the Brexit Adjustment Reserve
EIB Group financing in Cyprus in 2025, a record: €354 million of EIB loans and €18 million mobilised by the European Investment Fund
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Ten-year euro benchmark bond
register.detail: Public Debt Management Office · priced 21 January 2026 · due January 2036 · re-offer yield 3.339%, mid-swaps plus 44 bp · ISIN XS3281842578
register.note: Total demand above €16.4 billion, about 80% of it from international investors
register.text: A new ten-year benchmark bond of the Republic of Cyprus, €1 billion maturing in January 2036, listed on the London Stock Exchange under English law. The Minister of Finance stated that it replaces maturing debt and is not additional debt.

register.name: Inaugural sustainable bond, ten years
register.detail: Public Debt Management Office · April 2023 · coupon 4.125% · re-offer yield 4.219%, mid-swaps plus 125 bp · EMTN programme, listed in London
register.text: The first sustainable ten-year benchmark bond of the Republic of Cyprus, a €1 billion fixed-rate issue launched off its EMTN programme and listed in London under English law. Final demand exceeded €12.1 billion.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · €1,020M in grants, of which €52.4M from REPowerEU and €52.1M from the Brexit Adjustment Reserve · seventh-instalment decision 21 September 2026
register.note: The Commission now states €1,020 million, all in grants; estimated total cost of the amended plan €1,022 million
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Cyprus, including a REPowerEU chapter, paid in instalments as it meets its milestones and targets. The plan was amended again in 2026 with the EU financial contribution unchanged at €1,020,223,681; the Commission adopted its decision on the seventh instalment on 21 September 2026.

register.name: Cohesion Policy Programme THALIA 2021–2027
register.detail: European Commission · decision C(2026)1396 · final approval 4 March 2026 · ERDF, Cohesion Fund, ESF+ and Just Transition Fund · total public contribution €1,477M
register.note: The EU investment in the programme for 2021–2027; national co-financing makes up the rest
register.text: Cyprus’s cohesion policy programme for 2021–2027, funded by the ERDF, the Cohesion Fund, the Just Transition Fund and the European Social Fund Plus. Its objectives include sustainable water and waste and water management, active inclusion and employability, and addressing material deprivation; it serves the water, shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Cyprus Education Modernization Investment Plan
register.detail: EIB · project 20240887 · signed 18 December 2025 · Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth · total cost about €208M
register.note: More than 140,000 square metres of new and renovated school space
register.text: An EIB loan to modernise the school estate of Cyprus through new schools, extensions and renovations with energy efficiency measures, from pre-primary and primary to secondary and vocational education. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics (CING)
register.detail: EIB · additional €5M in 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Cyprus, 18 March 2026
register.note: Brings total EIB backing for the Institute to €31 million
register.text: Additional EIB financing for the Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics, which brings the Bank’s total backing for the Institute to €31 million. It serves the health standard through medical research.
by: Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics

register.name: EU funds co-financing 2021–2027 (THALIA structural programme loan)
register.detail: EIB · project 20220231 · approved 25 August 2023 · €130M signed 20 December 2023 · €50M signed 30 July 2025 · of about €369M proposed · total cost about €1,487M
register.note: Drinking water networks, sewerage, water supply replacements and smart water meters, among other sectors
register.text: An EIB structural programme loan for the national co-financing of priority investments under the THALIA programme 2021–2027, across energy, water and sewerage, solid waste, transport, education and health. It serves the water and shelter standards, among others.

register.name: National road network, second tranche
register.detail: EIB · second tranche of €100M, 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Cyprus, 18 March 2026
register.note: Highways, regional and rural roads, bridges, tunnels, and pedestrian and cycling infrastructure
register.text: The second €100 million tranche of EIB support for the national road network of Cyprus, covering highways, regional and rural roads, bridges, tunnels, and pedestrian and cycling infrastructure.

register.name: Wastewater management in Nicosia, Limassol and Larnaca
register.detail: EIB · signed 19 December 2023 · release of 22 December 2023 · sewerage boards of Nicosia and Limassol-Amathus and the Municipality of Larnaca
register.note: Sewer networks and treatment facilities, so that Cyprus complies fully with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive
register.text: An EIB loan for the preparation and construction of sewer networks and treatment facilities in Nicosia, Limassol and Larnaca, the three main cities of Cyprus, to help the country comply fully with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive. It serves the shelter standard, where safely managed sanitation is furthest from reach.

register.name: InvestEU guarantee for SME and start-up loans (Eurobank Ltd)
register.detail: European Investment Fund · launched 2025 · its first InvestEU guarantee with Eurobank Ltd · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Cyprus, 18 March 2026
register.note: Expected to mobilise loans of up to €62.5 million for SMEs and start-ups
register.text: A European Investment Fund guarantee under InvestEU that lets Eurobank Ltd lend more to small and medium-sized enterprises and start-ups in Cyprus; it is expected to mobilise loans of up to €62.5 million. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 16.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A pedestrian street of stone houses with bougainvillea and café tables in old Nicosia, Cyprus

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Pine forest on the ridges of the Troodos mountains in warm afternoon light, Cyprus

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Terraced vineyards and olive groves on sunlit foothills of the Troodos mountains, Cyprus

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A blue reservoir among dry golden hills with the Troodos mountains beyond, Cyprus

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A solar park on a dry plain with power lines leading towards the mountains, Cyprus

items.name: Food Connect (Friends of the Earth Cyprus)
items.text: A free app launched by Friends of the Earth Cyprus in July 2026 that lets hotels, restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets and food producers list surplus food that is safe to eat, for charities and the public to reserve and collect at no cost. It operates in Cyprus, Malta and Portugal under the EU Life programme, in a country with around 286 kg of food wasted per person a year.

items.name: Tylliria Energy Community
items.text: A not-for-profit energy community of the local councils of Kato Pyrgos, Pano Pyrgos, Pachyammos, Mosfili and Pigenia, registered in November 2025, that is installing solar panels and energy storage on about 200 buildings to reduce energy poverty through shared benefits. Over 100 applications for photovoltaic and storage systems were submitted in its first phase.

items.name: Agia Skepi Therapeutic Community
items.text: Cyprus’s first and only residential therapeutic community for people with long-term substance dependence, established in 1999, which supports its work through sales of its certified organic products in supermarkets and organic stores across Cyprus. Production gives its members work experience and vocational skills, and it employs programme graduates.

items.name: True Heart Café (Voice for Autism)
items.text: A café in central Nicosia, an initiative of the NGO Voice for Autism, that gives young people on the autism spectrum paid work and vocational training, with profits reinvested in training. Opened in May 2026 as the country’s first registered social enterprise, it employs 18 people with support needs who completed its training.
